text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000158 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation, but the returned charts largely support the billed level, so the pattern cannot yet be called upcoding or a legitimately complex panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"Against a legitimately complex panel: the 99215 share is roughly double the all-provider share in every complexity band, including 0–2 condition patients, so case mix alone does not explain the excess. For it: few 99215s fall on low-complexity patients, and 17 of the 18 documented 99215 claims show supporting high MDM (e.g., C0086503, C0086677). The one shortfall, C0086846, was on a four-condition patient. Two things limit the reassurance: records cover only about 6% of claims, and 29% of returned notes were flagged as duplicates, with no audit trail received. That raises the possibility that the supporting documentation is cloned rather than reflecting distinct encounters; the data-reviewed check found only one mismatch, so this remains a concern, not a finding. A reviewer should first compare the duplicate-flagged notes side by side (including the low-complexity 99215 C0086104, which also carries a problems flag), then request the audit trail and a larger chart sample weighted toward 99215s on 0–2 condition patients."}
